title: Choosing the Right Statistical Visualization
interviewAnswer: Choose charts based on the question: distributions, comparisons, relationships, composition or change over time. Favor position and length over harder-to-compare encodings and avoid decorative choices that distort magnitude.
why: Choosing the Right Statistical Visualization appears frequently in data-science work because it connects mathematical assumptions to practical decisions, diagnostics and failure modes.
deepDive: Choose charts based on the question: distributions, comparisons, relationships, composition or change over time. Favor position and length over harder-to-compare encodings and avoid decorative choices that distort magnitude. Scatter for numeric relationships. Bars for categorical comparisons. Lines for ordered time. A strong practitioner separates the modeling assumption from the estimation procedure, checks diagnostics rather than trusting a single score, and explains what would make the method inappropriate.
workedExample: Use an ECDF to compare latency distributions when tail behavior matters more than a single average.
commonMistakes: Applying the method without checking its assumptions or data-generating process.
Choosing it because it is familiar rather than comparing against an appropriate baseline.
followUps: What assumptions does Choosing the Right Statistical Visualization make?
How would you validate or debug Choosing the Right Statistical Visualization in practice?
production: In production, validate assumptions on real data, monitor the quantities that can drift, and keep a simple baseline so added complexity has a measurable reason to exist.

visual.title: Match mark to question
visual.caption: Position and length are usually easier to compare accurately than angle or area; choose encodings to match the analytical task.
